prerequisites: Solid foundations in computer science from the first semesters, including secure knowledge in formal mathematics (set theory, relations, functions, proof techniques, basic combinatorics).
Good programming skills and an understanding of algorithms and data structures.
Ability to comprehend abstract models like automata or Turing machines.
Enjoyment of formal precision, logical thinking, and abstract model building.

learning_outcomes.text: Students gain a comprehensive overview of the fundamental concepts and theories of theoretical computer science. They become familiar with different classes of automata and grammars, as well as the basics of computability and complexity theory. This knowledge forms the basis for a deeper understanding of computer science as a science, enabling abstraction.

Students specialize in the detailed analysis of core topics in theoretical computer science. This includes understanding the Chomsky hierarchy, the structure and function of various automaton types, and the fundamental principles of computability and complexity theory. The goal is to develop a profound understanding of these concepts.

Students should not only accumulate knowledge but also understand its application and significance in computer science. This includes recognizing connections between theoretical foundations and their practical application in algorithm development, language analysis, and solving complex problems.

Students learn to apply their acquired theoretical knowledge to practical problems. This involves the ability to choose and adapt appropriate theoretical models to solve problems in computer science. They should be able to use theoretical concepts to analyze, evaluate, and develop algorithms and software systems.

Students are encouraged to think beyond existing knowledge and develop their own research approaches. This includes the ability to critically question existing theories, formulate new hypotheses, and develop innovative solutions for theoretical and practical problems in computer science.

Students develop communication and teamwork skills. Students learn to communicate complex theoretical content understandably. Cooperative work on projects also promotes the ability to work in teams and exchange ideas.

Students develop an awareness of the importance and responsibility of theoretical computer science within science and society. This includes reflection on ethical aspects in research and application of computer science, as well as recognition of the role of theoretical computer science as a basis for innovations in technology.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Formal Languages and Automata based on the language classes of the Chomsky Hierarchy
assessment_rules: The graded examination can be an oral examination, a written examination, or a combination of a written examination and a multiple-choice examination. The duration and scope of these examinations are specified in the General Part of the Examination Regulations or the applicable study regulations.
